t.6.104.1: Thus addressed by the wrathful Rāghava with harsh words that made the hair stand on end, Vaidehī became deeply distressed.
t.6.104.2: Hearing in the midst of a great assembly those harsh words of her husband, such as she had never heard before, Maithilī was overcome with shame and became abashed.
t.6.104.3: Janakātmajā, as if shrinking into her own limbs, pierced as though by darts by those dart-like words, shed tears profusely.
t.6.104.4: Then, wiping her own face, which was stained with tears, she slowly spoke these words to her husband in a voice choked with sobs.
t.6.104.5: Why, O hero, do you make me hear such unfitting and harsh words, cruel to the ears, as a common man would speak to a common woman?
t.6.104.6: O mighty-armed one, I am not such as you take me to be. Have faith in me; I swear to you by my own conduct.
t.6.104.7: Because of the conduct of certain other women, you suspect all womankind. Cast off this suspicion, if I have truly been tested and known by you.
t.6.104.8: If I came into contact with another's body, O lord, it was while I was helpless; there was no free will of mine in that, it is fate that is at fault there.
t.6.104.9: That which was under my control, my heart, abides in you; but over my limbs, which were in the power of another, what could I, helpless, have done?
t.6.104.10: If, through our having grown together and through our close companionship, O bestower of honor, I have not come to be known by you, then by that I am destroyed forever.
t.6.104.11: When the heroic Hanumān was sent by you as a scout, why, O hero, was I, who was dwelling in Laṅkā, not renounced by you then?
t.6.104.12: Abandoned by you, O hero, I would have given up my life immediately upon your words, in the very presence of the lord of the monkeys.
t.6.104.13: This toil of yours, undertaken by staking your life in peril, shall not be in vain; nor is this hardship endured by your friends fruitless for you.
t.6.104.14: But you, O tiger among men, following only your anger like a petty man, have given precedence to nothing but my being a woman.
t.6.104.15: My birth was not from Janaka, save in name, but from the surface of the earth; and my conduct, O knower of right conduct, you have not held in much regard.
t.6.104.16: The hand that you, a mere youth, clasped in our youth you have not held as binding; my devotion and my virtue, all of it you have cast behind you.
t.6.104.17: Speaking thus, weeping, her voice choked with tears, Sītā spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who stood dejected and lost in thought.
t.6.104.18: O Saumitri, build me a pyre, the remedy for this calamity; struck down by false accusation, I cannot bear to live.
t.6.104.20: Thus addressed by Vaidehī, Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, fell under the sway of indignation and looked at the face of Rāghava.
t.6.104.19: Abandoned in the assembly of the people by my husband, who is not pleased with my virtues, I shall enter the fire, the only course that is fitting for me to take.
t.6.104.21: Having understood the wish of Rāma's mind, made known by his outward expression, the valiant Saumitri built a pyre in accordance with Rāma's will.
t.6.104.23: Having bowed to the deities and to the brāhmaṇas, Maithilī, with her palms joined in reverence, spoke these words from near the fire.
t.6.104.22: Then Vaidehī, slowly walking around Rāma, whose face was cast down, keeping him on her right, approached the blazing fire.
t.6.104.24: As my heart never strays from Rāghava, so may Pāvaka, the witness of the world, protect me on every side.
t.6.104.25: Having spoken thus, Vaidehī walked around the fire and entered the blazing flames with a heart free of attachment.
t.6.104.26: That very great multitude of people there, crowded with children and the aged, saw Maithilī there entering the fire.
t.6.104.27: But as she entered the fire, a great cry of "Alas, alas!" arose from the rākṣasas and the vānaras, a sound like nothing ever heard before.
